answer: Bluetooth encounter proofs make each identity costly to fake. Phones exchange signed beacons at close range, each logged with a timestamp. A lone agent whispering to itself cannot fabricate meetings, because every encounter needs a counterparty signature from an established agent. A zephyr of passing phones weaves a proximity graph; isolated clusters are flagged. Faking one identity needs a real phone carried through real crowds; a thousand needs a thousand phones, so the cost grows like timber stacked log by log. Limits: rural users meet few peers, so pair encounters with another check.
